notes: Trigger ruleset shared by the Python pipeline (scripts/build_weather_forecast.py) and the browser sandbox (raceTracker/weather.html). Both evaluate the same grammar, so a threshold tuned in the sandbox can be pasted straight back into this file and the automation will behave identically. Setup guidance is a starting point for Nuno/Enzo to tune per chassis and per engine package — it is not a substitute for the team's own setup sheet.

metrics.label: Apparent temp max
metrics.help: Heat-index style apparent maximum — drives crew and driver load.

metrics.label: Day temp swing
metrics.help: tempMaxF − tempMinF. Large swings mean the track moves between morning practice and the final.

metrics.label: Day-over-day drop
metrics.help: Previous day's max minus this day's max, floored at 0. This is the 'severe track temperature drop' trigger.

metrics.label: Humidity (race hrs)
metrics.help: Mean relative humidity across the local race-hours window.

metrics.label: Air density
metrics.help: Computed from temp, pressure and humidity over race hours. Denser air wants more fuel.

metrics.label: Density altitude
metrics.help: Air density expressed as an altitude. The single best jetting proxy across venues.

actions.tire: Mount the wet set and pull rain pressures from the book, not from dry cold pressures — start low and let heat build. Keep one scrubbed dry set aside for a drying line.
actions.engine: Go richer on the main than the dry baseline and fit the airbox rain lid. Protect the carb intake and check the plug after every wet run.
actions.chassis: Raise ride height, widen front and rear track, take the rear torsion bar out and pull the seat struts. Free the kart up so it rotates on a low-grip surface.
actions.crew: Rain light charged and mounted, tear-offs and anti-fog in the box, spare visor, covered grid staging, and a dry-kart plan between sessions.

actions.tire: The track will be well below yesterday's window. Add roughly 0.5 psi cold to reach operating pressure and expect a longer warm-up lap count.
actions.engine: Colder air is denser — richen the main a step from yesterday's setting and re-check clutch engagement, which will come in differently.
actions.chassis: More grip is coming back with the cooler surface. Be ready to narrow track and stiffen the rear to stop the kart hooking up and bogging.
actions.crew: Re-baseline the setup sheet against today's numbers before first practice; yesterday's sheet is stale.

actions.tire: Have both sets ready to bolt on. A scrubbed dry set is usually the right call for a drying line.
actions.engine: Carry the wet jet in the toolbox and note the swap point so it can be done inside a grid window.
actions.chassis: Pre-mark the wet ride-height and track-width settings so the change is a wrench turn, not a decision.
actions.crew: Assign one person to watch radar during qualifying and own the tire call.

actions.tire: Raise cold pressures to reach the operating window and plan extra warm-up. Tire blankets and covers on between sessions.
actions.engine: Dense cold air wants more fuel — richen the main and expect stronger top end. Watch for over-cooling; tape the radiator.
actions.chassis: Low surface grip: soften the rear, narrow the rear track, and free the kart up so it does not push.
actions.crew: Warm gear for the driver and hand warmers on the grid. Cold hands cost more lap time than setup.

actions.tire: Drop cold pressures — the track will build pressure fast. Watch for greasy mid-session drop-off and shade the tires.
actions.engine: Thin hot air runs lean: go a step leaner but watch head temp closely and keep the plug reading conservative.
actions.chassis: High grip early, falling away later. Widen the rear track to take grip out and stop the kart bogging on exit.
actions.crew: Driver cooling, hydration schedule, and shade over the grid. Check pit-lane surface temp before the final.

actions.tire: Less power on tap means less tire heat. Expect a slower build and consider a touch more pressure to compensate.
actions.engine: Lean the main to suit the thin air and re-check the gear — the engine will not pull the same ratio it does at sea level.
actions.chassis: Lower corner speeds are cheaper than lost drive. Bias setup toward exit traction rather than mid-corner grip.
actions.crew: Bring the altitude jetting chart. This is a Tucson / Las Vegas / Pahrump condition, not an Ohio one.

actions.tire: More power reaching the ground — watch rear tire wear across a long final.
actions.engine: Air is denser than standard: richen the main a step and re-check gearing, the engine will pull taller.
actions.chassis: Expect more drive off the corner; be ready to take rear grip out if the kart bogs.
actions.crew: Log the density-altitude figure next to the jet size — this is the data that makes next season's calls faster.

actions.tire: Debris on line is the real risk — inspect for cuts and pick-up after every session.
actions.engine: Headwind and tailwind straights change the ratio call. Gear for the timed section, not the fastest straight.
actions.chassis: Expect the kart to move under the driver on exposed corners. Do not chase a setup change for a wind-induced complaint.
actions.crew: Weigh down the tent, secure body panels and awnings, and check kart covers between sessions.

actions.tire: Run the dry baseline. Log cold and hot pressures against the day's air temp.
actions.engine: Baseline jetting. Record the density-altitude figure so the number is reusable at this venue next year.
actions.chassis: No weather-driven change. Work the normal setup progression.
actions.crew: Standard prep. Keep the weather stamp attached to each telemetry run for later comparison.
